output.normalized_title: ingress-lb: HTTP 500 spike reaching 42% of traffic (ingress-lb)

output.classification_reasoning: The ingress load balancer is returning HTTP 500 responses for a large portion of traffic (42%). A 500 status indicates an internal server error, which is typically caused by an application-level fault rather than network connectivity, authentication, or storage issues. The spike is observed in telemetry specific to the ingress-lb service, suggesting the failure originates within the load balancer's request handling or downstream application routing logic. The impact (150 users, 44 minutes) and the need to correlate telemetry, investigate request processing pipelines, and possibly roll back recent code changes imply a moderate level of operational effort, placing the incident in the 'Moderate' complexity tier.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: No direct historical incidents share the ingress-lb HTTP 500 spike symptom. The only related log is a WARN about replication lag on ingress-lb, suggesting a possible upstream database issue but insufficient evidence for a confirmed root cause.

output.justification: The incident affects 150 users, exceeding the 100‑user threshold for a moderate disruption. The outage duration of 44 minutes falls within the response window for Tier‑1 services, and the impact is limited to a single service (ingress‑lb) with no immediate evidence of a broader systemic failure. According to the corporate SLA matrix, a disruption of this magnitude and user count maps to SEV‑3. Therefore, the recommended SEV‑3 is confirmed.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Operator Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the executing engineer has the required ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
verification: AWS identity ARN includes ProdOperations role
kubectl context name contains prod-us-east-1

remediation_steps.title: Confirm Write‑Freeze State Before Node Operations
remediation_steps.description: Check that a write‑freeze is active on the primary database to prevent data loss during node reboot, and document the freeze timestamp.
commands: kubectl -n db get configmap write-freeze -o jsonpath='{.data.status}'
verification: ConfigMap status equals 'frozen'
RDS instance reports status 'available' with freeze flag set

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Elevate the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary database before tearing down the current primary node.
verification: New primary endpoint resolves to the replica instance
Application connection strings updated to point to new primary

remediation_steps.title: Gracefully Drain and Reboot Ingress‑LB Node
remediation_steps.description: Cordoned the node, evict pods, then perform a controlled reboot to clear any kernel‑level state that may be causing HTTP 500 spikes.
commands: kubectl cordon $(kubectl get nodes -l role=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl drain $(kubectl get nodes -l role=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
ssh -i ~/.ssh/prod_key $(kubectl get nodes -l role=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') sudo reboot
verification: Node shows NotReady during reboot and Ready after reboot
All ingress‑lb pods report READY=1/1 and are scheduled on the node

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Validate that the HTTP 500 rate has returned to baseline and that health‑check endpoints are healthy.
commands: kubectl logs deployment/ingress-lb -c controller --since=5m | grep 'HTTP 500' || true
verification: Error logs show < 1% 500 responses
Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
Metrics error_rate metric < 0.5%

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: If any verification step fails, revert the database promotion, undo the node reboot actions, and roll back the ingress‑lb deployment to the previous image tag while re‑enabling the write‑freeze.

verification: Original primary instance regains writer role
Application connection strings point back to original primary
Pods restart with previous image tag
kubectl rollout status deployment/ingress-lb shows successful rollout

steps.description: Cancel Node Reboot and Restore Node State
commands: kubectl uncordon $(kubectl get nodes -l role=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl get nodes $(kubectl get nodes -l role=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -o yaml > /tmp/node-backup.yaml
verification: Node reports Ready state
All ingress‑lb pods are scheduled and Running
ConfigMap status equals 'frozen'

prerequisite_checks: Write‑freeze status confirmed before any node reboot
Rollback procedures documented and approved by change management
